items.stem: A 2-D array has rows as samples and columns as features. To compute the mean of each feature, which axis should be aggregated?

options.text: axis=0 (down the rows, one result per column)
options.rationale: Correct: aggregating over axis=0 collapses the rows, giving one mean per feature column.

options.text: axis=1 (across the columns, one result per row)
options.rationale: axis=1 collapses columns, giving a per-sample mean, not per-feature.

options.text: Either axis gives the same result
options.rationale: The axes produce different results for a non-square, non-symmetric array.

options.text: NumPy ignores the axis for mean
options.rationale: The axis argument directly controls which dimension is reduced.

items.explanation: Correct: aggregating over axis=0 collapses the rows, giving one mean per feature column.

items.stem: A basic slice of a NumPy array is modified and the original array changes too. What explains this?

options.text: Basic slicing returns a view that shares memory with the original
options.rationale: Correct: a basic slice is a view over the same buffer, so edits propagate.
Basic slicing returns a view, not a copy.
dtype does not determine view-versus-copy behaviour.
Broadcasting is unrelated to why a slice shares memory.

items.explanation: Correct: a basic slice is a view over the same buffer, so edits propagate.

items.stem: Which TWO are reasons to vectorise code with NumPy instead of using Python loops? (Select TWO)

options.text: Operations run in optimised compiled code over whole arrays
options.rationale: Correct: ufuncs push the loop into fast compiled code, avoiding per-element Python overhead.

options.text: It typically reduces interpreter overhead per element
options.rationale: Correct: vectorised ops avoid the per-iteration Python bytecode cost.

options.text: It guarantees results are always more numerically precise
options.rationale: Vectorisation changes speed, not inherent numerical precision.

options.text: It removes the need to consider array shapes
options.rationale: Shape and broadcasting still matter when vectorising.

items.explanation: Correct: ufuncs push the loop into fast compiled code, avoiding per-element Python overhead.
